description: [capability-version: 0.9.84] Capability for document windows only. Settings and PDF-export windows have separate, restricted capability files. SECURITY NOTE: Filesystem permissions use broad path patterns because VMark is a document editor that must access user-chosen files anywhere on disk. These broad grants are constrained at the application layer, per surface: (1) image embed paths are CLASSIFIED, not confined, by validateImagePath() in src/plugins/shared/mediaSecurity.ts — it refuses a URI scheme, a home-relative path and a directory-naming path, but it does not bound which FILE a document may address, because absolute paths are converted one branch earlier with no validation. What an embed can actually LOAD is bounded by the RESOLVED path: the assetProtocol scope in tauri.conf.json is these same static roots (plus C:\ to F:\ via tauri.windows.conf.json), extended at runtime only for files and folders the user opened. It stopped refusing `..` in 0.9.79 (#1433): the check broke the standard `../images/photo.png` layout while blocking nothing an absolute path could not already reach; (2) MCP-bridge file operations (workspace.open/save/save_as and document.write) via resolveBridgePathDecision() in src/utils/mcpBridgePathPolicy.ts, which confines bridge reads/writes to the open workspace root and open-document directories. Direct human-driven file flows (Open/Save dialogs) rely on the OS file picker for path selection. A RUNTIME grant satisfies every fs permission below, write and remove included, so recursive (folder) grants are made only in src-tauri/src/workspace/grants: the folder picker Rust shows, a folder opened from Finder, or a root recorded from one of those. Windows drive letter patterns are in a separate windows.json capability file.
